title: Evaluation of Translation Rate Through AHA Incorporation and Click Chemistry in Yeast
author: Mainak Pratim Jha
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Yeast strain BY4741 (genotype: MATa his3Δ1 leu2Δ0 met15Δ0 ura3Δ0; parent strain: S288C; source: S288C/EUROSCARF) Reagents
Yeast nitrogen base (Himedia, catalog number: M
Agar powder, bacteriological grade (Himedia, catalog number: GRM
Note: Light sensitive, store at -20 °C, prepare dilutions right before use as a stressor in cultures.
Sodium phosphate dibasic (MP Biomedicals, catalog number:
Potassium phosphate dibasic (MP Biomedicals, catalog number:
EDTA disodium dihydrate (MP Biomedicals, catalog number:

steps.title: Prepare synthetic complete agar plates
steps.instruction: Streak a glycerol stab of BY4741 onto a synthetic complete (SC) agar plate, incubate 4–5 days at 30 °C, then store at 4 °C; prepare SC agar by autoclaving 53 % (v/v) agar in water, add sterile‑filtered media components, adjust volume, pour while warm, let solidify.

steps.title: Inoculate primary overnight culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony into 5 mL SC liquid media in a 25 mL capped glass flask and grow overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.

steps.title: Inoculate secondary cultures
steps.instruction: Dilute the overnight culture into four 25 mL flasks each containing 25 mL SC media to an initial OD₆₀₀ = 0.1; grow at 30 °C, 200 rpm until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.4–0.6 (≈5 h). Assign flasks to untreated control, heat stress, tunicamycin stress, and cycloheximide stress.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Transfer each culture to a 50 mL centrifuge tube, spin 3,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in sterile autoclaved water, spin again 3,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend in AHA medium
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in synthetic complete medium in which methionine is replaced by L‑azidohomoalanine (final 0.02 mg/mL AHA) and transfer to fresh 100 mL capped conical flasks.

steps.title: Add stressors
steps.instruction: Add tunicamycin to the designated flask to a final concentration of 2.5 µg/mL and cycloheximide to a final concentration of 50 µg/mL; leave the untreated and heat‑stress flasks unchanged.

steps.title: Incubate stress treatments
steps.instruction: Incubate untreated, tunicamycin‑treated, and cycloheximide‑treated flasks at 30 °C, 200 rpm; incubate the heat‑stress flask at 37 °C, 200 rpm. Perform both 6 h and 24 h incubations for short‑ and long‑term stress.

steps.title: Normalize cell density and harvest
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of each culture, adjust volumes to reach a target OD₆₀₀ = 1 (or ≥20 OD for protein extraction). Transfer the required volume to 50 mL tubes, spin 8,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature, keep the pellets for downstream steps.

steps.title: Wash cells in water
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 1 mL autoclaved water, transfer to 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, spin 8,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells with ethanol/PBS
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in 1 mL of 53 % (v/v) ethanol in 1× PBS, incubate at 15 °C with shaking at 200 rpm for 40 min.

steps.title: Wash after permeabilization
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 8,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Perform click labeling
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL click reaction buffer containing Tris‑Cl 2 M (final 200 mM, pH 8.5), CuSO₄ 50 mM, Alexa‑Fluor 488 alkyne 1 µg/mL, and sodium L‑ascorbate 500 mM; incubate at 30 °C, 200 rpm for 30 min.

steps.title: Wash post‑click reaction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 8,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Aliquot cells for downstream assays
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 1 mL 1× PBS; take 10 µL for confocal microscopy, 100 µL for flow cytometry, keep the remainder for protein extraction. Centrifuge the remaining suspension 8,500 × g for 5 min at room temperature and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % agarose pads
steps.instruction: Make 1 % agarose in 1× PBS, pour onto glass microscope slides, allow to dry forming bubble‑free pads with appropriate moisture.

steps.title: Mount cells on agarose pads
steps.instruction: Place the 10 µL microscopy aliquot onto a prepared agarose pad, cover with a clean coverslip.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Image using a Nikon A1R MP+ confocal microscope with a 100× oil‑immersion lens, 488 nm laser, gain 200, offset ‑25, laser power 5, TD detector gain 125, and a 3‑fold digital zoom (total 300×). Include a scale bar.

steps.title: Load samples for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Place each 100 µL cell aliquot into a fresh microcentrifuge tube and load onto a Beckman Coulter Cytoflex‑S cytometer.

steps.title: Set cytometer acquisition settings
steps.instruction: Configure FSC gain 45, SSC gain 40, Alexa‑Fluor 488 alkyne gain 90; acquire 50,000 events per condition.

steps.title: Lyse cells with NaOH
steps.instruction: Resuspend each cell pellet in 600 µL 0.3 M NaOH solution, incubate upright at room temperature for 10 min.

steps.title: Remove NaOH supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 1,500 × g for 1 min at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend in protein storage buffer
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL protein storage buffer (10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 7.4, 1 mM EDTA, 150 mM KCl, 1 mM PMSF) to the pellet.

steps.title: Add glass beads
steps.instruction: Add 300 mg acid‑washed glass beads to each tube.

steps.title: Bead‑beat cells
steps.instruction: Using a Bead‑Ruptor, vortex at level 3 for 3 min, then place tubes on ice for 3 min; repeat for a total of four cycles (12 min total vortexing).

steps.title: First clarification spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysates at 16,900 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, transfer the supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Second clarification spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collected supernatant at 16,900 × g for 30 min at 4 °C; keep the cleared protein extract on ice or store at ‑20 °C.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of each extract using a BCA assay.

steps.title: Add SDS loading dye
steps.instruction: Mix each extract with 5× SDS loading dye to achieve a final 1× loading dye concentration.

steps.title: Denature samples
steps.instruction: Boil the dye‑mixed samples at 95 °C for 15 min with intermittent vortexing.

steps.title: Spin down denatured samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 2 min at room temperature and retain the supernatant.

steps.title: Cast 10 % polyacrylamide gel
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel using standard protocols and include a stain‑free imaging reagent.

steps.title: Load samples onto gel
steps.instruction: Load 10 µL of each boiled sample into a single lane of the gel.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run the gel at a constant 100 V until the tracking dye front exits the gel.

steps.title: UV‑activate stain‑free gel
steps.instruction: Expose the gel to UV light for 5 min to activate the stain‑free reagent.

steps.title: Image gel fluorescence
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence of the gel (488 nm excitation) using an iBright gel documentation system; newly synthesized proteins appear as green bands.

steps.title: Image total protein load
steps.instruction: Capture a UV image of the same gel using a Bio‑Rad EZ documentation system to visualize total protein loading.

description: Validation of protocol From the initial stage, we maintained three independent biological replicates of our yeast strain for both primary and secondary inoculation, which were consistently utilized across various experimental setups, including confocal microscopy, flow cytometry analysis, and protein extraction followed by SDS-PAGE analysis. In the confocal microscopy procedure, we captured five distinct fields for each replicate, resulting in a total of 15 microscopic image fields per treatment condition. For flow cytometry analysis, three individual replicates were retained for each treatment condition, with 50,000 cells (events) recorded per vial, culminating in a total of 1,50,000 cells for each treatment condition. In the whole-cell protein extraction and SDS-PAGE analysis, three individual replicates were maintained for each treatment condition, with only one replicate presented in Figure 5 for illustrative purposes. Statistical significance was assessed using a T-test for pairwise comparisons between treatment conditions and untreated controls. The significance indicators and their corresponding values are detailed in the figure legends, where the statistical tests are depicted within the plots. In this experimental protocol aimed at determining the translation rate of actively growing yeast cells, unstressed cells served as a positive control, where protein synthesis occurred at a natural rate, while cycloheximide was employed as a negative control to completely inhibit translation. The data presented in the figures confirm that the positive control exhibits translation, whereas the negative control demonstrates a cessation of translation. This protocol (or parts of it) has been used and validated in the following research article: • Jha et al. [6]. Sse1, Hsp110 chaperone of yeast, controls the cellular fate during endoplasmic reticulum stress. G3 – Genes, Genomes, Genetics ( Figure 3b ).
